evidence.quote: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) issues this circular to inform licensed corporations that it will exempt non-centrally cleared single-stock options, equity basket options and equity index options (collectively, “non-centrally cleared equity options”) from its margin requirements1 from 4 January 2026 until further notice to align with the latest global developments.
1 As set out in Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Code of Conduct).

arguments.inference: On the expressly questioned transaction facts, give the announced commencement date effect without adding prior gazettal as a condition. Applicability is a defeasible conclusion for that assumed assessment, not an established real-world exemption or a determination of overall compliance.

premises.explanation: The circular identifies its addressed population but does not establish the assessed corporation's licensing status. That status is assumed for this argument.
The footnote identifies the regime, but does not establish that this corporation's transaction would otherwise fall within it.

Assume a listed non-centrally cleared option assessed on or after 2026-01-04 with no effective notice displacing this exemption for it. None of these transaction-specific facts is established by the packet; missing evidence is not falsity.

evidence.quote: Paragraph 7(e) of Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course.

arguments.inference: For the same assumed assessment as arg.applicability, if gazettal is constitutive and its commencement requirements remain unmet at that date, infer that the announced exemption is not yet operative. The source establishes neither assumption, so this alternative remains conditional.

evidence.quote: Paragraph 7(e) of Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course.

premises.explanation: Amendment and gazettal are described as future steps at the time of the circular, not necessarily at the assessment date.
The alternative assumes that gazettal is legally constitutive. The supplied text does not state that requirement.
For the hypothetical assessment, assume that the required gazettal and commencement conditions remain unmet. Their status on any actual assessment date is unknown.

attacks.rationale: Under its questioned constitutive-gazettal and assessment-date assumptions, arg.gazettal concludes the negation of arg.applicability's defeasible conclusion for the same assessment. It supplies no negative inference-applicability proposition, so it is not an UNDERCUT.

evidence.quote: Paragraph 7(e) of Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course.

preferences.rationale: Provisionally prefer arg.applicability, supported by arg.scope, as an interpretation of the announced commencement: it gives effect to the express date without adding an unstated prerequisite. This does not verify its factual assumptions or independent legal force. Arg.gazettal survives as a conditional legal alternative because the underlying Code and implementation instruments are unavailable.

questions: What evidence establishes the assessed corporation's licensed status and the otherwise applicable Part III of Schedule 10 obligation? The circular establishes neither transaction-specific premise.
What evidence establishes the option category, clearing status and assessment date assumed in p.app.factual_conditions?
Has any subsequent notice effectively displaced this exemption for the assessed transaction? Absence from the packet establishes neither continued applicability nor its negation.

Is gazettal constitutive of legal effect, and were any required amendment and commencement conditions unmet on the assessment date? The circular's future-tense statement alone does not answer either question.
Do the missing Code provisions or implementing instruments prescribe additional scope qualifications, reporting obligations or transitional treatment?
The unsupported self-UNDERMINE and malformed UNDERCUT have been removed. Factual uncertainty remains in the questioned premises; it does not justify concluding their negations.
